Definition: from G5056 and G5608; a tax-farmer, i.e. collector of public revenue:--publican.
BiblicalUsage: The word is a publican, a collector of the Roman taxes, hated by his own people. Jesus saw Levi sitting at the receipt of custom and said, Follow Me; the publican stood afar off and would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner; and Jesus says the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom before the chief priests.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the publican's prayer is the prayer God hears, and the tax collector goes in before the priest who trusts himself.
